newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, COURIER ADVANCE IN PHILADELPHIA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, COURIER ADVANCE IN PHILADELPHIA.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras extended his current winning streak to 16 matches on Wednesday with a first-round straight sets victory at the Advanta Championships.
The top-seeded Sampras took 56 minutes to brush past Marcelo Filippini of Uruguay 6-4 6-1.
Second seed Jim Courier followed Sampras by opening defence of his title with a 6-3 7-6 win over 89th-ranked Guillaume Raoux of France.
Sampras, who has twice won this tournament, got off to an erratic start, making an inordinate number of errors and struggling to find a rhythm with his serve.
"I concentrated pretty well, so it was okay, but I didn't serve well in the first set," Sampras said.
"My serve was a little bit up and down in the beginning," added the Australian Open champion, who won his first career title here in 1990 at age 18.
Sampras finally found his form in the ninth game of the first set, completing a love game with two sizzling service winners and an ace.
He then captured the first set by breaking the 79th-ranked Filippini at 30-40 on a winning forehand approach shot.
"It took me awhile to settle down," Sampras said. "It came together when I served that love game and had a good set point."
Sampras totally dominated the second set, allowing Filippini to hold serve only once in the second game.
The 18th-ranked Courier was tested by Raoux in the one hour and 33 minute match.
Leading 5-2 in the second set, the former number one failed to close out the match and was pushed to a tiebreaker by Raoux.
In the tie-break, Courier jumped out to a commanding 6-1 lead but again had trouble closing out the match, squandering his first three set points, including two on his own serve.
"I got it done although I would have preferred to close it out earlier," admitted Courier.
"Still, bottom line is to get the W (win)."
